description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, generously studded with a vibrant assortment of fresh seafood and crisp green onions. Its irresistible crispy edges and tender interior make it a perfect appetizer or light meal, often enjoyed with a tangy dipping sauce. This traditional dish offers a delightful balance of flavors and textures, truly a taste of Korea's coastal bounty.

ingredients.notes: shrimp, squid, mussels, small octopus, cleaned and chopped

instructions.title: Prepare the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, and black pepper. Add the cold water and egg, then whisk until just combined. Do not overmix; a few lumps are fine and will ensure a lighter pancake texture. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Clean and chop your mixed seafood into bite-sized pieces. Cut green onions into approximately 3-inch lengths. Thinly slice the half onion and the optional red chili. Ensure all ingredients are ready for assembly.

instructions.title: Make the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, optional gochugaru, and minced garlic. Stir well and set aside. This sauce perfectly complements the savory pancake.

instructions.title: Cook the First Pancake
instructions.text: Heat 1-2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, pour about 1 cup of batter into the pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Immediately arrange half of the prepared seafood, green onions, and sliced onions evenly over the batter.

instructions.title: Crisp the Bottom
instructions.text: Cook the pancake for about 5-7 minutes, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, and the edges begin to set. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges of the pancake to help crisp it up further.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Carefully flip the pancake using a wide spatula. Cook for another 5-7 minutes on the second side, pressing gently with the spatula to ensure even cooking and crispiness. The seafood should be cooked through and the pancake golden brown on both sides.

instructions.title: Repeat and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, transfer the Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Repeat the process with the remaining batter and ingredients to make a second pancake. Slice the finished pancakes into wedges and serve immediately while hot, with the prepared dipping sauce on the side.

tips: For extra crispiness, use very cold water for the batter and add a tablespoon of cooking oil directly into the batter.
Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook one pancake at a time to ensure even heat distribution and a perfect crisp texture.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking to enjoy its best texture. It tastes best when hot and crispy.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to Korea and discover the delightful world of Haemul Pajeon, a savory seafood and scallion pancake that has captured the hearts and palates of food lovers worldwide. This iconic dish is more than just a pancake; it's a celebration of fresh ingredients, vibrant flavors, and the comforting essence of Korean home cooking. Whether you're seeking a hearty snack, a flavorful appetizer, or the perfect accompaniment to a glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine), Haemul Pajeon promises an unforgettable gastronomic experience. Its crispy edges, tender interior, and generous medley of seafood and aromatic scallions make it a truly irresistible treat.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon translates directly to "seafood scallion pancake," with "haemul" meaning seafood and "pajeon" referring to a scallion pancake. It is a beloved variety of *jeon*, a general term for Korean savory pancakes made from various ingredients mixed with a flour-based batter and pan-fried. Unlike thinner, crepe-like pancakes, *pajeon* are typically thicker, showcasing a substantial amount of their main ingredients, especially the signature long green scallions.

What sets Haemul Pajeon apart is its generous inclusion of a diverse array of fresh seafood, which often includes plump shrimp, tender squid, mussels, and sometimes clams or oysters. These ingredients are bound together by a light, crispy batter and cooked until golden brown, resulting in a dish that is both satisfyingly crunchy on the outside and wonderfully soft and flavorful on the inside. It's particularly popular on rainy days, a tradition stemming from the sizzling sound of the pancake mimicking the sound of falling rain, making it an ideal comfort food.

## Ingredients You Need for Haemul Pajeon

Crafting the perfect Haemul Pajeon starts with selecting fresh, high-quality ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

*   **For the Batter:**
    *   1 cup all-purpose flour (for extra crispiness, you can substitute 1/4 cup with rice flour or cornstarch)
    *   1 large egg
    *   1 to 1 1/4 cups ice-cold water or anchovy broth (cold liquid is key for crispiness!)
    *   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   **For the Vegetables:**
    *   2-3 bunches green onions (scallions), about 10-15 stalks, cut into 3-4 inch lengths
    *   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced (optional, but adds sweetness)
    *   1/4 cup shredded carrot (optional, for color and slight sweetness)
    *   1-2 fresh green or red chilies, thinly sliced (optional, for a kick)
*   **For the Seafood:**
    *   1/2 lb mixed seafood: shrimp (peeled, deveined, cut into bite-sized pieces), squid (cleaned, scored, and cut into rings or pieces), mussels or clams (cleaned and shelled)
*   **For Pan-Frying:**
    *   Vegetable oil or any neutral cooking oil, generously
*   **For the Dipping Sauce (recommended):**
    *   2 tablespoons soy sauce
    *   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
    *   1 teaspoon sesame oil
    *   1 teaspoon sugar
    *   1 clove garlic, minced
    *   1 teaspoon sesame seeds
    *   A pinch of red chili flakes (gochugaru)

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon: Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Haemul Pajeon at home is surprisingly straightforward, yielding incredibly delicious results. Follow these steps for a perfect pancake:

**Step 1: Prepare Your Ingredients.**
Thoroughly wash and pat dry all your seafood. Cut shrimp and squid into bite-sized pieces if they aren't already. Prepare your vegetables: cut the scallions into 3-4 inch lengths, thinly slice the onion, and shred the carrot if using. Mince the garlic for the dipping sauce.

**Step 2: Make the Batter.**
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, salt, and egg. Gradually add the ice-cold water or broth, whisking until the batter is smooth but slightly lumpy. Be careful not to overmix, as this can develop gluten and make the pancake chewy instead of crispy. The consistency should be like a thin pancake batter.

**Step 3: Combine Ingredients (or Layer).**
Gently fold most of the prepared seafood and scallions into the batter. If you prefer a more artful presentation, you can reserve some seafood and scallion pieces to arrange on top of the pancake once it's in the pan.

**Step 4: Pan-Fry the Haemul Pajeon.**
Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring the bottom of the pan is well coated. Once the oil is hot (it should shimmer), pour about 1 cup of the batter mixture into the pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake, about 1/2 inch thick. If you reserved some seafood and scallions, quickly arrange them on top of the batter in the pan.

**Step 5: Cook and Flip.**
Cook for 3-5 minutes on the first side, or until the edges are golden brown and crispy, and the top begins to set. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges. Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Cook for another 3-5 minutes on the second side, pressing down gently with the spatula to ensure even cooking and crispiness. The goal is a deep golden-brown crust.

**Step 6: Serve Immediately.**
Once both sides are beautifully golden and crispy, transfer the Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice it into wedges or squares, and serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more oil to the pan as needed for each pancake.

## Pro Tips for the Best Crispy Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that perfect crispy exterior while maintaining a tender interior is the hallmark of a great Haemul Pajeon. Here are some expert tips:

*   **Ice-Cold Batter:** This is perhaps the most crucial tip. Using ice-cold water or broth, or even adding an ice cube to your batter, inhibits gluten development, resulting in a lighter, crispier pancake.
*   **Don't Overmix:** A few lumps in your batter are perfectly fine. Overmixing activates gluten, leading to a tough, chewy pancake instead of a light and crispy one.
*   **Generous Oil:** Don't be shy with the oil! Haemul Pajeon needs a good amount of oil to fry properly and develop that coveted crispy crust. You should hear a satisfying sizzle when the batter hits the pan.
*   **High Heat to Start:** Begin cooking on medium-high heat to quickly crisp the exterior. Once flipped, you can reduce the heat slightly to medium to ensure the interior cooks through without burning the outside.
*   **Press Down Gently:** After flipping, gently press the pancake with your spatula. This ensures even contact with the hot pan, promoting uniform crispiness.
*   **Thin is In:** For maximum crispiness, aim for a relatively thin pancake. A thicker pancake will be softer and less crispy.
*   **Single Layer Cooking:** Avoid overcrowding your pan. Cook one or two pancakes at a time, depending on your pan size, to maintain consistent heat and ensure proper browning.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is typically enjoyed fresh off the pan, when it's at its crispiest and most aromatic.

*   **The Dipping Sauce:** A simple yet essential dipping sauce elevates the flavors of the Haemul Pajeon. Whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, minced garlic, and sesame seeds. A pinch of red chili flakes adds a pleasant warmth. This sweet, savory, and tangy sauce beautifully complements the rich seafood and savory batter.
*   **Beverage Pairings:** Traditionally, Haemul Pajeon is a quintessential pairing with *makgeolli*, a milky Korean rice wine. The slight fizziness and mild sweetness of makgeolli cut through the richness of the pancake, making for a harmonious combination. Soju or a cold beer are also excellent choices.
*   **As an Appetizer or Main:** Serve it as a delightful appetizer for a Korean meal, or as a light and satisfying main course alongside other Korean side dishes (*banchan*). It’s also perfect for a casual get-together or as a comforting snack on a chilly evening.

## Variations and Substitutions for Your Haemul Pajeon

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a masterpiece, there's plenty of room for customization to suit your taste or dietary preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** Easily made vegetarian by omitting the seafood entirely. Increase the amount of scallions and consider adding other vegetables like sliced mushrooms (shiitake or oyster work well), zucchini, bell peppers, or even kimchi for a savory, tangy twist.
*   **Kimchi Pajeon:** For a spicy and sour kick, add about 1/2 to 1 cup of chopped kimchi (well-drained) to your batter. This variation, known as Kimchi Jeon, is incredibly popular.
*   **Meat Additions:** Some variations include thinly sliced beef or pork (often marinated) along with, or instead of, seafood.
*   **Flour Blend:** Experiment with different flour ratios. Adding a small amount of glutinous rice flour or cornstarch to your all-purpose flour can enhance crispiness and chewiness.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the spice by adding more or fewer fresh chilies to the batter, or a dash of gochugaru (Korean chili powder).
*   **Broth Flavor:** Using anchovy broth (dasima 육수) or vegetable broth instead of water for the batter will impart a deeper, umami-rich flavor to your Haemul Pajeon.

Whether you stick to the traditional recipe or get creative with variations, mastering Haemul Pajeon is a rewarding culinary achievement. It's a dish that brings warmth, flavor, and a touch of Korean hospitality to any table. So gather your ingredients, fire up your pan, and get ready to enjoy one of Korea's most beloved savory treats!
